description: Mixed attention effect (row 2, smaller attention field). Two solid CRFs: attended (thick) plateaus ABOVE unattended (thin); separation persists at high contrast (attended ~0.74, unattended ~0.61; neither reaches 1.0). Dashed percent-modulation (right axis) is largest at low contrast (~93%) and declines monotonically to a ~21% plateau at high contrast, crossing the rising solids near mid contrast.

provenance.figure_type: line/curve CRF, log-x, two solid sigmoids (left axis, attended thick > unattended thin, both sub-1.0) plus one descending dashed (% modulation, right axis)
provenance.tool_rationale: Mode-1 quantitative plot. detect_plot_box for the axis-rectangle hint; verified by longest-dark-run profile. trace_darkest_in_band, one band per solid by row; the dashed isolated as the topmost cluster at low contrast (it starts highest, ~93%, and descends). resample_pchip for the flat plateaus; overlay for the single validation pass.

calibration.axis_lines_measured: left axis col 57.5 (NOT the label-text edge ~col 41), right axis col 189.5, plot top row 23.5, bottom row 202 — read off the longest-consecutive-dark-run profile.

per_curve.attended: upper-right solid cluster centroid per column; rises later/steeper, plateaus ~0.74. Clearly separable from unattended through the rise and at the plateau (the panel's whole claim).
per_curve.unattended: lower solid cluster centroid; plateaus ~0.61, distinctly below attended at every contrast.
per_curve.percent_modulation: dashed, traced as the topmost cluster at low contrast (~93% peak), descending monotonically; past x~0.07 it falls below the rising solids and crosses them, after which the topmost-cluster tracer picks up a solid, so the descending tail (to the ~21% plateau) is read from the dashed's own band below the solids and PCHIP-joined through the crossover.

provenance.normalization: paper shared sub-1.0 scale; attended plateau ~0.74, unattended ~0.61, NOT pinned to 1.0; the attended>unattended height difference (the panel's claim) is preserved. Right axis % modulation 0-100 read independently.
provenance.calibration_note_vs_prior_audit: The 2026-06-03 audit's 'rising-flank-too-high / c50-too-low' finding for 3F traces to the same wrong left-axis column (41.5, the tick-label edge) used in that audit instead of the true axis line col 57.5. Re-checked with the correct calibration, the solid attended rising-flank values match the true pixel cluster centroids to within ~0.01 (e.g. x=0.0871 -> y 0.541 measured vs 0.542 prior; x=0.0707 -> 0.465 vs 0.466). The solid CRFs were already faithful; this pass re-verifies them with recorded anchors.
caveats: No numeric x ticks (only Log Contrast tick marks); x_range [0.01,1.0], 2 log decades, from the frame, consistent across 3A-3F.

Dashed crossover (x~0.05-0.10): where the descending dashed crosses the two rising solids the three same-colour lines bundle; the dashed there is PCHIP-interpolated through the bundle rather than column-traced (minor, ~+/-2%).
Right-axis % modulation calibration assumes the right tick frame shares the plot top/bottom rows (no legible intermediate numeric ticks).
provenance.re_digitization_2026_06_04: X-AXIS RE-LABELED to the AUTHOR contrast window [1e-5, 1] (paper/code/attentionModel/Figure3F.m cRange=[1e-5 1]; CODE-013/014/015/018). The paper panel has NO numeric x ticks, so the prior pass guessed the left frame edge at 0.01 (2 decades); the authors' script axis floor is 1e-5. The CURVE INK on the paper is unchanged - this is a pure x-axis frame RELABEL: each traced point keeps its exact pixel position, its contrast value is recomputed from the SAME log-fractional position across the frame under the author window (c_new = lo*(hi/lo)^f, f = the point's fractional log-x position in the old frame).
